chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: The Armstrong sextet

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: How long did you know him before that?
Oh years. I knew Louie back in 1936, so that was '36 up to '49, 13 years prior to that.
Had you ever played with him before?
On record dates, one. But not regular like that every night, you know. Yeah, but that was a great little job. People used to come and hear us. I think that that was one of the best bands that

Louie had, quintets, with Earl Hines, Jack Teagarden, Barney Bigard, Arvell Shaw, Louie and me. And Velma Middleton singing. People used to come and hear us and said, well we better go hear this band tonight, because no telling how long they're going to be together. Jack Teagarden was the first one that left, I think Earl Hines left later, then me. That's how the band broke up, but all in all, we were all together, that personnel, that same band for about five years, and it was really tight. It was a good band. Yeah, that was a good band.
